title: TVC attitude control: pole-placement PID vs LQR
description:
Thrust-vector attitude hold during the boost: the flight computer keeps the nose on the launch-rail direction using the strapdown/magnetometer attitude estimate and one gain-scheduled PID per plane, tuned by pole placement (zeta 0.7, wn 8-18.5 rad/s, integral pole -4) on the linearised short-period model. Control is active from rail exit to the start of the thrust tail-off (3.97 s); after that the gimbal is centred and the rocket coasts to apogee.

Variants show the transient response with and without disturbance (wind, turbulence, a side gust and thrust misalignment), and the closed loop with estimation + actuation delay inside (15 + 15 ms) and beyond (30 + 30 ms) the delay margin. Each plot overlays the passive (gimbal locked) rocket in the same conditions.

LQR variants compare an LQR attitude controller against the pole-placement PID in the same conditions (margins table from gnc.lqr).

variants.notes: Disturbance: 10 m/s wind from the West (1/7 shear), 3 m/s turbulence, 4 m/s 1-cos side gust at 1.5 s, 0.25 deg thrust misalignment per axis. Holding a fixed attitude in a crosswind means fighting the weathercock moment: the AoA equals wind/V, which is large at low speed (over 30 deg just off the rail, with the rail tilted downwind). The gimbal sits at its 5 deg limit for about half of the guided window, while the integral action trims the misalignment out. The passive rocket instead turns into the wind (large pointing deviation, small AoA). Holding the attitude costs gimbal authority and effort.

variants.notes: 15 ms actuation + 15 ms estimation delay (30 ms loop delay plus ~6 ms intrinsic) is inside the Pade delay margin for most of the boost (56 ms mid-boost, 33 ms at TVC end). The response is almost identical to nominal. Configured loop delay 30 ms.

variants.notes: 30 + 30 ms (66 ms loop delay incl. intrinsic) exceeds the delay margin at every operating point. The closed loop is unstable: a gimbal oscillation grows steadily (0.1 deg at 1 s, ~1 deg at 2.5 s, >4 deg at 3.8 s, close to the 5 deg limit) and the attitude error and effort grow several-fold. It stops only because the TVC is switched off at tail-off (3.97 s); a longer burn would end in saturation. Configured loop delay 60 ms.

variants.notes: LQR attitude controller (gnc.lqr: Bryson weights theta 4 deg, q 40 deg/s, integral 0.3 s, delta 5 deg on [theta, q, int e], gain-scheduled at the same 9 points; it is a PID with LQR-chosen gains), nominal conditions. The first two plots overlay the pole-placement PID in the same conditions. Without delay the LQR holds the attitude tighter, with less gimbal effort (and, in the disturbance case, no saturation where the PID saturates half the time). The table shows the price: its delay margin is only ~28 ms during the first ~2 s (PID 55-73 ms), and its integral trim is slower (settling up to ~6 s at TVC end). The 15 + 15 ms delay variant (~36 ms with the sim's intrinsic delay) therefore oscillates under LQR while the PID is unaffected. The PID's wn floor tracks the airframe frequency, which is what keeps its early-boost delay margin large.
